clue.text: Interrupting in the governing body with a point is stupid

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another word, so the point goes inside the governing body

parts.note: the Senate is a governing body, as in Rome or the US
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone barging in on a council meeting just to make a point is behaving foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interrupting' signals the point breaking into the governing body; the surface's meeting-room scene hides that 'in' is simply its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Insensate means senseless or without understanding, hence foolish.

clue.text: Fashionable scoundrel covers debit-vouchers — how careless!

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that covers another sits on top of it, so it comes first

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a cur is a contemptible, cowardly man
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A trendy rogue scribbles IOUs everywhere, and the writer tuts at his carelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' puts IN and CUR above IOUS in the down light. 'how' is a link word introducing the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Incurious means lacking interest or attention, so careless or indifferent.

clue.text: Place to sit or stand in the market

definitions.meaning: a seat in a church choir or the front seats of a theatre
a trader's booth or table at a market

explanation.definitionFit: Theatre and choir seats are both called by this word, as is a market trader's booth.

clue.text: Respirators supplied, naturally!

parts.note: the breathing apparatus here is not a machine but the openings nature gives every face

explanation.definitionFit: The nose's two openings take in air for breathing, so they are the body's own breathing devices.

clue.text: Any crest, displayed with a difference, indicates ancient lineage

indicators.note: the letters of the words are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A heraldic crest, shown with a variation, reveals an old family line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed with a difference' rearranges ANY CREST; in heraldry a 'difference' is a mark distinguishing a branch of a family, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent from forebears over many generations is one's family line.

clue.text: Book departure from Egypt

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Old Testament
the Israelites' flight out of Egypt led by Moses

explanation.definitionFit: The Bible book is named after the Israelites' mass flight from Egypt, which it tells.

clue.text: Press agency gets nothing from poet

parts.note: TASS was the Soviet news agency
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A news agency gets no story out of a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquato Tasso was a sixteenth-century Italian poet, author of Jerusalem Delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso wrote the epic Jerusalem Delivered, making him an Italian poet.

clue.text: Speculation caused by the opening of overhead railway

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: People guess at what happened when an elevated railway line was opened.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a conjecture or supposition, an idea not yet proved.

clue.text: Siamese coat-maker gets a tip

parts.note: the seal grows a fur coat prized for sealskin
a point is a sharp tip

explanation.surface: A tailor from Thailand who makes coats is given a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: A sealpoint is a Siamese cat with dark brown points (ears, face, paws, tail).
explanation.definitionFit: Sealpoint is a colour variety of the oriental cat breed, pale with dark brown extremities.

clue.text: Old convict's German prison

parts.note: an old lag is British slang for a habitual convict, and the possessive 's is read as 'of'
an old lag is British slang for a habitual convict, and the possessive 's is read as 'of'

explanation.surface: A former inmate recalls a jail in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old convict's' is read as 'of (old) lag': the possessive turns into OF, and LAG is the convict. Oflag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for officers.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oflag was a Second World War camp in Germany where captured officers were held.

clue.text: Derby, for example, is unromantic but extremely important

definitions.meaning: the Derby is one of the five English flat-racing ...
classical in style rather than romantic, and also of the first rank

explanation.surface: A famous horse race is described as unsentimental yet hugely significant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is one of the great annual flat races; the word also means restrained in style and of lasting excellence.

clue.text: It should give total protection for the worker

definitions.text: It should give total protection for the worker

parts.words: It should give total protection for the worker
parts.note: a protective garment worn over clothes at work, which also means total or all-inclusive

explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece work garment covering the clothes; the same word means comprehensive or total.

clue.text: Chief measure used in line-drawing

definitions.meaning: a head of state such as a monarch
a straight-edged strip marked in inches or centimetres

explanation.surface: The boss sizes things up with a straightedge when drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign governs a country; the same word names the graduated straightedge for drawing lines.

clue.text: Margaret is old-fashioned and a misfit

parts.note: square is slang for conventional or old-fashioned
Peg is a pet form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret is behind the times and doesn't fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsuited to their situation is likened to a squared shape in a round hole.

clue.text: US standard secondhand gyro — could be about a pound

parts.note: something secondhand is old

indicators.note: the letters could be put in another order

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: An American buyer weighs a used gyroscope, guessing it at about a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges GYRO into GORY, and 'about' puts L inside it to make GLORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Glory is a nickname for the Stars and Stripes, the American flag.

clue.text: What Scott found in the Thames?

definitions.text: What Scott found in the Thames?

parts.words: What Scott found in the Thames?
parts.note: the explorer's Antarctic ship, which was then moored on the Thames in London, but also any find an explorer makes

explanation.walkthrough: Captain Scott's ship RRS Discovery was moored on the Thames in London for decades; the clue pretends Scott made a find there.
explanation.definitionFit: A find is a discovery, and Robert Falcon Scott's polar ship bore that name.

clue.text: Unused sauce

definitions.meaning: in perfect condition, as a stamp or coin never used
a sharp herb sauce served with lamb

explanation.definitionFit: Collectors call an untouched stamp or coin in perfect condition by this word; it is also a herb sauce served with lamb.

clue.text: Dockers cut can be a bit of a fiddle

definitions.meaning: those who dock an animal cut off part of its tail
the piece on a violin to which the strings are fixed at the lower end

explanation.definitionFit: Docking an animal removes part of its tail; on a violin, the strings are anchored on this piece.

clue.text: Member of a society — the Woodworkers?

definitions.meaning: the Ancient Order of ... is a British friendly society
a person who works in and manages woodland

explanation.surface: A member of a club joins the carpenters' guild.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland keeper works among trees; members of a British friendly society, a mutual insurance club, bear the same name.

clue.text: The side's hero, maybe, though all at sea

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: The team's star player is completely bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges HERO into HORE. 'All at sea' looks like confusion but means literally out on the water; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Located away from the coast, out on the water rather than on land.

clue.text: Waistband for light frame?

definitions.meaning: a band of cloth worn around the waist
the frame holding the glass in a window that lets in light

explanation.definitionFit: A decorative band worn round the waist, and the glazed frame of a window share one name.

clue.text: Bits of paper etc if not collected, are found after the match

indicators.note: the letters are gathered up and put together afresh

explanation.surface: Scraps of paper left lying around after a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' rearranges ETC IF NOT. The 'match' is a wedding, after which the paper scraps are found.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pieces of coloured paper thrown over a newly married couple.

clue.text: Mimic Bobby? That's right!

parts.note: a bobby is a British policeman, named after Sir Robert Peel
i.e., id est, means 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the impressionist is doing a policeman, and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: One who imitates another is a mimic or imitator.

clue.text: Put money into a modish waistcoat

parts.note: in means fashionable
in American English a vest is a waistcoat

explanation.surface: Someone spends cash on a stylish waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to commit funds in the hope of profit.

clue.text: You or I, for example, go to church to make declaration

indicators.note: one piece goes on to join the next

parts.note: 'you' and 'I' are personal pronouns
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Ordinary people go to church to make a solemn statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to declare formally, as a judge pronounces sentence.

clue.text: Sound and true

definitions.meaning: to measure the depth of water with a weighted line
exactly vertical, as a builder's line hangs

explanation.definitionFit: Plumbing the depth means measuring with a lead weight; a wall that is exactly vertical is also described by the word.

clue.text: The Educational Supplement is in type

parts.note: the Times Educational Supplement, the teachers' weekly, is known by the initials TES, which the answer read as an instruction produces

explanation.surface: The teachers' weekly is being typeset.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: put SET 'up', that is, backwards, and it gives TES, the initials of the Times Educational Supplement; the phrase also means typeset.
explanation.definitionFit: Text that has been set up has been composed in type, ready for printing.

clue.text: Dance-beat followed with vigour

indicators.note: the first piece is followed by the second

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A rhythm is danced energetically.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Reunite somehow children of mixed parentage

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective describing such children: born of the same mother but different fathers

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Bring a blended family back together somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges REUNITE. Uterine siblings share a mother but not a father.
explanation.definitionFit: Uterine brothers or sisters have the same mother and different fathers, so different parents on one side.

clue.text: Worst right back, once high-class centre

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation is read in reverse
the high-class letter is placed inside the word once

parts.note: U means upper-class

explanation.surface: Someone was beaten to the right and back, once at the heart of polite society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the abbreviation for right; 'centre' places U, the old shorthand for upper-class, inside ONCE after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To worst a rival is to defeat them soundly.

clue.text: In his market supplies are cheap and plentiful

definitions.text: In his market supplies are cheap and plentiful

parts.words: In his market supplies are cheap and plentiful
parts.note: the economist's phrase for a market where goods are abundant favours whoever purchases

explanation.definitionFit: A market with plentiful cheap supplies favours the purchaser, hence 'a buyer's market'.

clue.text: Company has no existence in this group

definitions.text: Company has no existence in this group

parts.words: Company has no existence in this group
parts.note: the proverb 'two's company, three's none' says company vanishes once a third person joins

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'Two's company, three's none' (or 'a crowd') says that when a third joins, company ceases.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three people, the number at which the proverb says company ceases.
